chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Arriving at Club Alabam and the Downbeat on Central Avenue
summary: First night on Central Avenue and the layout of the Downbeat, his all-time favorite club.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We went into Lincoln, Nebraska to play...and the next stop was Los Angeles (hah-hah-hah!) at the Club Alabam on Central Avenue between 42nd and 42nd Place. And I never will forget it. We got in in the middle of...oh, somewhere about 11:30 or 12 o'clock. And Central Avenue was just full of people. All kind of things were happening, you know. They had The Last Word across the street, and Dynamite Jackson's down the street.

They had the Downbeat on 42nd and Central, which is my all-time favorite Jazz club that I played in, because it was really made for it. Black-Dot McGee was the owner at the time. And he had really laid this place out; it was perfect for Jazz, you know.

Well, it was made like a box. The bandstand was against one wall, and they had a long bar in front of the bandstand, but it had mirrors all the way across, so the people sitting at the bar didn't have to turn around, you see -- because they could look at you in the mirrors and see the stage. And it was about 8 inches high, which is just

plenty high enough, because you're down there with the people, and people on both sides of you and in front of you -- you're surrounded! So it was a warm feeling. You know, you were really communicating. And it wasn't too big. And the sound was good, everything...
